A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inv-Entropy research, with matching core methods and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison, including identification of relocated material and genuine additions or removals.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-3.5-Turbo and LLaMA experiments, including benchmark scores, TSU results, and perturbation, embedding, replication, and bootstrapping analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds evaluated Kernel Entropy comparisons, computational-cost measurements, and NQ answer-length results.

M1.justification: The Inv-Entropy computation, Algorithm 1, and GAAP procedure remain unchanged. However, Section 2.3 changes the stated marginal P(X) from pi_uniform P_y P_y P_x to pi_uniform P_y P_x despite retaining its defining distributions. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents an intended change to marginal-based variants or a formula error.

E1.justification: The same five datasets and three task categories remain. v2 specifically reports evaluation on NQ questions with only long-form reference answers, spanning 34–350 tokens, including length-specific subsets; v1 described concise reference answers without this reported scenario. The TriviaQA-to-SciQ caption correction in v1 Table 8 versus v2 Table 11 does not establish added coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Kernel Entropy, distinct from the retained Kernel Language Entropy, to Table 1 and the selected TSU comparisons in Table 2. It also removes the complete LLaMA comparison against the UQ baselines previously reported in v1 Table 9. The retained LLaMA figure compares perturbation and embedding variants, so cross-model baseline validation is substantially reduced.

E3.justification: The added NQ analysis groups reference answers into Short (<80 tokens), Medium (80–120), and Long (>=120). The new cost comparison measures peak GPU memory and separates post-processing time from total time, averaged over TriviaQA questions without parallelization. Existing correctness metrics, TSU definition, and shared inference settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds answer-length sensitivity analysis in Table 6, resource-cost analysis in Appendix D.2/Table 4, and a generated-response case study contrasting replication with perturbation in Figure 1. These investigate applicability, computational burden, and confidently wrong responses. The existing bootstrapping, replication, embedding, and temperature ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same 40 bootstrap resamples for evaluation means and standard deviations in Appendix D.1. There is no changed seed or repeated-run design, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing. Renaming the method's bootstrap count from S to B does not change statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the NQ results: Inv-Entropy's AUROC/PRR/Brier values change from 0.703/0.764/0.182 to 0.661/0.614/0.201 under v2's explicitly long-answer setting, not an established same-setting deterioration. v2 adds Kernel Entropy, answer-length, and cost results and removes v1's LLaMA Table 9. Several TSU values also change, including Semantic Entropy on TriviaQA at TSU(0.7,1.4), from 17.35 to 20.64. The retained ablation tables have identical numerical values.

T1.justification: New Section 2.5 derives conditional monotonicity of Inv-Entropy with output dispersion for a restricted symmetric-similarity model, assuming diagonal conditional probabilities below 1/e. Appendix B restores the missing factor of two in Equation (14)'s cross term while retaining the original lemma. Section 2.3 also changes the marginal formula, introducing an inconsistency with the retained Equations (3)–(4).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's five contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a flexible probabilistic inverse framework, justification for perturbations, GAAP, TSU, and strong empirical performance. Wording changes and additional supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly describes Inv-Entropy as unnormalized, adds interpretations of answer-length dependence, and expands the computational-cost discussion to API-call scaling and parallelization. It acknowledges weaker performance on longer answers. However, its accompanying claim of consistently ranking among the top two overstates Table 6: Inv-Entropy's Long-subset PRR of 0.508 ranks fourth.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 newly documents the (n+1)r response-call count, timing components, and measured memory/runtime requirements. Conversely, v1's disclosure of 1,000 sampled examples per dataset disappears without replacement. The shared prompts, perturbation and replication settings, A100 hardware statement, and code-access information remain; the missing sample count does not establish an actual sample-size change.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gruber and Buettner's Kernel Entropy work and removes the Shafer–Vovk conformal-prediction reference and associated contrast with model-free UQ. Appendix A's related-work taxonomy and the central novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the motivation, random-walk and inverse-distribution exposition, bootstrapping explanation, and evaluation narrative are rewritten. v2 changes 'calibration-based' terminology to 'correctness-based,' adds an insights subsection and appendix outline, and reorganizes appendix commentary alongside its tables. These are substantial exposition and structural revisions beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds the response-example figure, redraws the level-set illustration, and expands the random-walk caption. The full TSU table moves to Appendix Table 5 while a compact main-text Table 2 is introduced. New cost and answer-length tables are added, and the LLaMA benchmark table is removed. The GAAP diagram and perturbation/embedding bar chart are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful answer-length and cost evidence, another baseline, clearer explanations, and a corrected proof step. However, it removes the complete LLaMA comparison and per-dataset sample-count disclosure, while introducing a marginal-probability inconsistency and conflicting TSU summaries: MMLU WD-px-py is 22.54 in Table 2 versus 21.65 in Table 5. The gains in explanation and diagnostic evidence coexist with weakened validation and reporting reliability, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
